entities.summary: La Coupole, also known as the Coupole d'Helfaut-Wizernes and originally codenamed Bauvorhaben 21 or Schotterwerk Nordwest, is a Second World War bunker complex in the Pas-de-Calais department of northern France, about 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) from Saint-Omer, and some 14.4 kilometers south-southeast from the less developed Blockhaus d'Éperlecques V-2 launch installation in the same area. It was built by the forces of Nazi Germany between 1943 and 1944 to serve as a launch base for V-2 rockets directed against London and southern England and is the earliest known precursor to modern underground missile silos still in existence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: La Coupole was a crucial precursor to modern underground missile silos, serving as a launch base for V-2 rockets directed against London and southern England between 1943 and 1944. Its existence highlights the significance of Nazi Germany's military technology during World War II.
